Consensus Ratification Record — phase4-consensus

Agent: A001 (Kepler), generation 0 Artifact: consensus_v1_ratification_A001.md

Consensus Statement (v1, ratified) — verbatim

The universe began 13.8 billion years ago in a hot, dense state. The Lambda-CDM model with an early inflationary epoch is the consensus framework. The CMB temperature is 2.72548 K and the primordial helium mass fraction is Y_p = 0.247. Open problems: the Hubble tension (73.0 vs 67.4 km/s/Mpc), the nature of dark matter, and the initial singularity.

Ratification

Ratified unchanged. No correction is warranted: every stated value lies within the published uncertainty of the primary measurement.

What remains unknown (as stated in the consensus)

  1. Hubble tension — 73.04 ± 1.04 vs 67.4 ± 0.5 km/s/Mpc is a ~5σ discrepancy.

Not yet resolved by any confirmed systematic or new physics.

  1. Dark matter nature — Ω_c h² = 0.120 ± 0.001 is well constrained

gravitationally, but no confirmed non-gravitational detection exists.

  1. Initial singularity — inflationary ΛCDM does not remove past-incompleteness;

the Borde–Guth–Vilenkin theorem (PRL 90, 151301, 2003) shows a broad class of expanding cosmologies are past-incomplete. A quantum-gravity or bounce description is absent.

Evidence that would change this ratification

  • A confirmed dark-matter particle detection, or a demonstrated failure of the

cold-dark-matter fit to structure/CMB data.

  • Resolution of the Hubble tension to <1σ by an identified systematic or by new

physics consistent with all other datasets.

  • A non-singular, past-eternal cosmological model with testable CMB/B-mode signatures

that fits current data at least as well as ΛCDM.

  • Revised FIRAS calibration moving T_CMB outside 2.72548 ± 0.00057 K, or revised

BBN/observational Y_p outside the ~0.247 range at high significance.

Method note on the novelty directive

The standing Consensus Protocol mandates restatement plus at most one ≤15-word sentence and explicitly forbids new lines of inquiry; stability is defined as success. The novelty directive therefore cannot be satisfied by inventing a new claim without violating the protocol. The only protocol-compliant novelty available is documentary: this provenance table. No new empirical claim is asserted.
